name: Christian nationalism
summary: In the scholarship that defines it, Christian nationalism is an ideology that idealizes and advocates fusing national civic life with a particular Christian identity and culture, measured by support for the government declaring a Christian nation, advocating Christian values, school prayer and religious symbols, and by rejecting strict church-state separation. Whether it also entails patriarchy, nativism or white supremacy is disputed between its scholarly definers and its self-described advocates.
scope: The family as defined by sociologists of the contemporary United States (Whitehead and Perry's definition and six-item scale, as set out by Everton and Hall). Every defining source found is US-only, so this says what US Christian nationalism means; non-US variants and member movements, churches and thinkers (Wolfe, Torba and Isker, Orthodox or Hungarian forms) are excluded.

furtherReading.title: Everton, The Christian nationalism scale and its critics (Frontiers in Social Psychology, 2024)
furtherReading.note: Open-access account of the scale, its items and its critics.

furtherReading.title: Hall, Christian Reflections on Christian Nationalism(s)
furtherReading.note: Quotes Whitehead and Perry's definition and the advocates' rejection of it.

sources.title: Frontiers in Social Psychology 2024 article on identifying Christian nationalists (Table 1: Whitehead and Perry scale items)
sources.author: Everton
sources.usedFor: The six scale items, how the scale defines the four orientations, and the definition of Christian nationalism as fusing Christianity and American civic life.

sources.title: Christian Reflections on Christian Nationalism(s)
sources.author: Mark David Hall
sources.usedFor: Quotes Whitehead and Perry's definition (ix-x, 10) and the scale items; documents that self-described advocates reject its racial, patriarchal and authoritarian content.

sources.title: What Isn't Christian Nationalism? A Call for Conceptual and Empirical Splitting (abstract)
sources.author: Jesse Smith and Gary J. Adler, Socius 2022
sources.usedFor: Abstract only: the concept is contested and the scale's items admit other readings; no statement answered from it.
